cues.text: Good Morning. Youth Council. Caroline speaking.
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: Oh, hello, I’m interested in standing for election to the Youth Council, and I was told to give you a call.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: That’s good. Could I have your name, please?
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: Yes, it’s Roger Brown.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: Thank you. I’m Caroline, the Youth Council administrator. So do you know much about what the Council does, Roger?
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: I’ve talked to Stephanie – I think she’s the chair of the Council.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: That’s right.
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: And she told me a lot about it. How it’s a way for young people to discuss local issues, for example, and make suggestions to the town council. That’s what made me interested.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: Fine. Well let me take down some of your details. First of all, how old are you? You know the Council is for young people aged from 13 to 18?
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: I’ve just turned 18.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: And where do you live, Roger?
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: Well, that’s a bit complicated. At the moment I’m looking for a flat to rent here, so I’m in a hostel from Monday to Friday. I go back to my parents’ place at the weekend.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: OK, so where’s the best place to send you some information about the Council?
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: Oh, to my parent’s address, please. That’s 17, Buckleigh Street – B-U-C-K-L-E-I-G-H Street, Stamford, Lincolnshire, though you don’t really need the county.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: Oh, I know Stamford – it’s a lovely town. And what’s the postcode?
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: PE9 7QT
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: Right, thank you. So are you working here, or are you a student?
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: I started studying at the university a couple of weeks ago, and I’ve got a part-time job for a few hours a week.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: What do you do?
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: Well, I’ve done several different things. I’ve just finished a short-term contract as a courier, and now I’m working as a waiter in one of the big hotels.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: Uhuh. That can’t leave you much time for studying!
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: Oh, it’s not too bad. I manage to fit it all in.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: What are you studying?
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: My ambition is to go into parliament eventually, so my major subject is politics. That’s partly why I think the Youth Council is important and want to be a part of it.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: And I suppose you’re also taking a minor subject, aren’t you? I know a lot of people study economics too.
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: I chose history. To be honest, I’m not finding it as interesting as I expected!
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: OK, so with your studying and your part-time job, do you have time for any other interests or hobbies?
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: Well, I spend quite a lot of time cycling – both around town to get to university and to work, and also long-distance, from here to London, for instance.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: That’s pretty impressive! Anything else?
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: For relaxation I’m also keen on the cinema – I used to go at least once a week, but I can’t manage to go so often now.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: Right. Are you sure you’ll have enough time for the Youth Council?
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: Yes, I’ve worked out that I can afford to reduce my hours at work, and that will make the time.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: So is there any particular aspect of the Youth Council’s work that appeals to you, Roger?
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: Well, my sister is blind, so I’m particularly interested in working with disabled young people, to try and improve the quality of their lives.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: That’s great. Well, the best way to get involved is to be nominated by some people who you know.
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: Right. Can you tell me how to set about organising that?
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: You should talk to Jeffrey, our Elections Officer. I can arrange a meeting in the council office with him, if you like.
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: Yes, please.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: He’ll be here next Monday, if that suits you
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: That’s the 14th, isn’t it?
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: Yes.
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: I can manage late afternoon.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: Would you like to suggest a time? He generally leaves around 5.30.
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: Well, would 4.30 be OK? My last class finishes at 4, so I’d have plenty of time to get to your office.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: Right, that’s fine. Oh, and could I have a phone number we can contact you on?
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: Yes, my mobile number’s 07788 136711.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: Thank you. Well, we’ll look forward to seeing you next week.
cues.speaker: CAROLINE

cues.text: Thanks very much. Goodbye.
cues.speaker: ROGER

cues.text: Bye.
cues.speaker: CAROLINE
